thread:
Nina: Follow-up on operator-local admission for dedicated GPU pools. Idea: small signed manifest + local circuit-breaker so shims can return 'provisional' instead of hard 429s. minimizes control-loop chatter during drains.
Arjun: Sounds good. main risk is policy drift; manifest must be canonical and versioned.
Maya: plan: CP compiles signed manifest (epoch + tiny bitmap + thresholds). shim honours it, emits shim.manifest_epoch and shim.provisional_count.
Nina: what about fallback ordering? prefer local reroute -> quantized_variant -> cpu_proxy -> reject. keep it configurable in manifest.
Arjun: add cooldown_ms and max_provisional_streak to avoid oscillation.
Maya: agreed. also require shim to refuse unknown major epoch and fall back to conservative reject with shim.manifest_mismatch=true.
DevBot: DeployBot: manifest epoch 2025-05-10T11:30Z signed by Maya and staged to canary at 2025-05-10T11:45Z :rocket:
Nina: telemetry: shim.provisional_rate, shim.circuit_open_gauge, shim.fallback_chain span tag. autoscaler should subscribe to provisional_rate and circuit_open to trigger emergency scale-ups.
Arjun: compatibility check must be O(1) on hot path (bitmap or 8-byte hash). avoid RPCs.
Maya: rollout: 5% canary -> 30m observe provisional_rate & fallback_quality -> gradual rollout + automated rollback if provisional_rate spikes above threshold. I'll draft RFC follow-up with manifest proto + shim API.
Nina: great, thanks. small security note: shim verifies manifest signature via KMS before applying.
Maya: will include that.
